For the exact-real recurrence, write $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for positive integers $m,n$. Let $p_1,\ldots,p_m>0$ be source probabilities summing to one, let $d_{ij}\ge0$ be finite distortions for $(i,j)\in[m]\times[n]$, let $\beta\ge0$ be finite, and let $q_0$ be any full-support reproduction pmf. For $t=0,1,\ldots$ set
$$
Z_i(q_t)=\sum_{j=1}^n q_t(j)e^{-\beta d_{ij}},\qquad W_t(j\mid i)=\frac{q_t(j)e^{-\beta d_{ij}}}{Z_i(q_t)},\qquad q_{t+1}(j)=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iW_t(j\mid i).
$$
All denominators are positive, every row of $W_t$ sums to one, and $q_{t+1}$ has full support. Define the nats objective $L_\beta(W)=I_{\rm nat}(X;\widehat X)+\beta\mathbb E d(X,\widehat X)$, the current channel value $L_t=L_\beta(W_t)$, and the a-posteriori factor
$$
\gamma_t:=\max_{1\le j\le n}\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\frac{e^{-\beta d_{ij}}}{Z_i(q_t)}\ge1.
$$

For $\tau>0$, the output is the first processed iteration index $t$ for which a rigorous upper interval endpoint $u_t\ge\ln\gamma_t$ satisfies $u_t\le\tau$, together with $W_t$, $q_{t+1}$, $L_t$, and interval enclosures of these values and $\ln\gamma_t$. Compute the objective by
$$L_t=\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n p_iW_t(j\mid i)\ln\frac{W_t(j\mid i)}{q_{t+1}(j)}+\beta\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n p_iW_t(j\mid i)d_{ij}.$$
The exact-real recurrence defines all values being enclosed.

The certified interval procedure is defined only when every $p_i,d_{ij},\beta,q_0(j)$ and $\tau$ is rational, with the positivity, normalization, finiteness and full-support conditions above and $\tau>0$. Execute the following loops. For $t=0,1,2,\ldots$, try precisions $r=2,3,4,\ldots$ in order. At precision $r$, use the dyadic format $(p,e_{\min},e_{\max})=(r^2,-r,r)$ and truncation index $N=r$ in [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]]. Round each rational input outward to an interval in this format. Build a finite typed expression DAG for the recurrence from $q_0$ through $q_t$, and request enclosures for every $W_t(j\mid i)$, $q_{t+1}(j)$, $L_t$, and $s_{j,t}:=\sum_i p_i e^{-\beta d_{ij}}/Z_i(q_t)$. If rounding any input overflows or the evaluator returns a non-finite status, increase $r$ and repeat this precision loop. Otherwise form the interval $G_t=[\max_j\underline{s}_{j,t},\max_j\overline{s}_{j,t}]$ from the rational endpoints of the $s_{j,t}$ enclosures, and evaluate $\ln G_t$ with the same format and truncation index. If this evaluation is non-finite, increase $r$ and repeat. Continue increasing $r$ until all requested output enclosures, including that of $\ln\gamma_t$, have width less than $1/(t+1)$. Let $u_t$ be the upper endpoint of the resulting $\ln G_t$ enclosure. If $u_t\le\tau$, return the stated output and enclosures; otherwise end the precision loop and proceed to $t+1$. For arbitrary exact-real inputs the recurrence remains mathematically defined, but this interval implementation is specified only under the rational representability conditions. No bit-complexity bound is asserted.

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.
For finite probability vectors $p,q$ on the same alphabet, $D(p\|q)\ge0$, and $D(p\|q)=0$ if and only if $p=q$. If $p_i>0=q_i$ for some coordinate, then $D(p\|q)=+\infty$.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of functions
$n \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on it
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). Then:

1. **Closed boxes are compact.** For reals $a_k \le b_k$ $(k < n)$ the box
   $Q = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_k \le x_k \le b_k \text{ for every } k < n \,\}$
   is a compact subset of $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
2. **Heine-Borel.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ if and only if $K$ is closed in $\mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-topology]]) and bounded
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).
3. **The real line.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}, d_{\mathbb{R}})$, the usual metric $d_{\mathbb{R}}(x,y) = |x-y|$
   ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]), if and only if $K$ is closed in
   $\mathbb{R}$ and bounded.

**No choice principle is used.** The bisection below halves one coordinate at a
time and takes the **left** half whenever the left half still fails to be finitely
covered, the right half otherwise: a rule with two outcomes, decided by a
property of the box, not a selection. That is the whole reason the theorem is
available in ZF, while the general "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]) is not.

The hypothesis $n \ge 1$ is inherited from [[lem-metrics-on-rn]], which defines
$\mathbb{R}^n$ and its metrics only there; the last remark below records what
happens at $n = 0$.

Let $(X,d)$ be a nonempty compact metric space ([[def-metric-compactness]],
[[def-metric-space]]) and let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous
([[def-metric-continuity]]), $\mathbb{R}$ carrying its usual metric
$d_{\mathbb{R}}(s,t) = |s-t|$ ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]). Then the
image $f[X]$ is bounded above and below ([[def-bounded-set]]), and it has a
maximum and a minimum ([[def-max-min]]): there are points
$x_{\max}, x_{\min} \in X$ with

$$f(x_{\min}) \;\le\; f(x) \;\le\; f(x_{\max}) \qquad \text{for every } x \in X,$$

and then $f(x_{\max}) = \sup f[X]$ and $f(x_{\min}) = \inf f[X]$
([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-infimum]]).

Nonemptiness of $X$ is a hypothesis and not an oversight: for $X = \emptyset$ the
image is empty and has neither a supremum nor a maximum. No choice principle is
used.

Input: a finite, well-formed, typed expression DAG with one or more designated
output nodes; finite real interval or complex rectangle assignments for its
input nodes; exact dyadic constants or constants supplied with certified
enclosing intervals/rectangles; a finite dyadic format $(p,e_{\min},e_{\max})$
with $p\ge2$ and $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$; and an integer truncation index
$N\ge1$. Input interval endpoints and supplied constant enclosures use this
format. All constants, including every Machin enclosure of $\pi$, use the
same fixed $N$ and format throughout a call. Real nodes support input and
constant nodes and the operations $+,-,\times,\div,\sqrt{\phantom{x}},
\exp,\ln,\arctan,\sin,\cos,\tan$. Complex nodes support input and constant
nodes and $+,-,\times,\div,\exp,\operatorname{Log}$. Each operation has
homogeneous real or complex inputs of its stated type; no implicit conversion
between real and complex nodes is performed. Unsupported node types, arities,
or type combinations return `inconclusive` with the offending node.

Output: a finite interval/rectangle enclosure for every designated output
node, or one of `empty`, `entire`, `domain-error`, `split-domain`, `overflow`,
or `inconclusive` with the node and unresolved domain piece. If any supplied
input is `empty`, return `empty`. No value from a system `libm` routine is
treated as a certified endpoint. Each DAG node is evaluated once; shared nodes
reuse their interval/rectangle enclosure and do not preserve correlations
between distinct paths.

1. Check that node identifiers are unique, all references resolve, every
designated output is a node, and the supported node types and arities above
hold. Use each supplied input enclosure as its node value. For an exact real
dyadic constant $c$, use $[\operatorname{rd}(c),\operatorname{ru}(c)]$ in the
selected format. For an exact complex dyadic constant, do this to each
coordinate. A finite subnormal endpoint remains a valid endpoint; if a
coordinate conversion overflows, return `overflow` with that constant node.
Use a supplied certified constant enclosure as given. Construct a topological
order by repeatedly removing a node whose
predecessors have already been removed, breaking ties by lexicographically
smallest node identifier. If no such node exists before all nodes are ordered,
return `inconclusive` with a node in the cycle. Evaluate nodes in this order
and store each finite enclosure for its successors. Arithmetic nodes use
[[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]]; if an operation returns
a non-finite status, propagate it immediately with its node and unresolved
piece. For $\sqrt{X}$ require $X\subseteq[0,\infty)$ and for $\ln X$ require
$X\subseteq(0,\infty)$; otherwise return `domain-error` rather than silently
discarding points.

2. For a real exponential node, set $s=\max(0,e_{\max}+2)$ using the format
in [[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]]. Since
$N_{\max}<2^{e_{\max}+1}$, exact comparison gives $N_{\max}/2^s<1/2$. For
its input interval $X$, form the exact dyadic interval $U=2^{-s}X$
without storage rounding. Evaluate the degree-$N$ exponential polynomial and
add the symmetric tail from
[[lem-range-reduced-exp-log-and-arctan-series-enclosures]], using
$\max_{u\in U}|u|<1/2$, by exact rational interval arithmetic. Round only
the resulting interval endpoints outward, then square that interval $s$ times. If its lower
endpoint is not positive or an endpoint overflows, return `inconclusive` or
`overflow` with the node and input interval.

For a real logarithm node, first require $X\subseteq(0,\infty)$. List all
integers $j$ for which $X_j=X\cap[2^j,2^{j+1}]$ is nonempty; exact endpoint
comparisons find this finite list because $X$ has positive finite endpoints.
On each piece form $Y=2^{-j}X_j\subseteq[1,2]$ and $V=(Y-1)/(Y+1)$
by exact rational endpoint formulas without storage rounding, so
$V\subseteq[0,1/3]$. Evaluate the logarithm polynomial and its tail
determined by $\max|V|$ by exact rational interval arithmetic, round the
result outward, and form $j\ln2+\ln Y$ by outward arithmetic. Compute the fixed enclosure for
$\ln2$ once by the same series and tail at $y=2$, hence $v=1/3$, and reuse it
in every bin. If any piece cannot be evaluated finitely, propagate its status
and that piece. Otherwise take the interval hull of all piece enclosures as
the node enclosure.

3. Partition a real arctangent input at the fixed breakpoints
$-3,-1,-1/2,1/2,1,3$ into nonempty closed pieces, allowing shared endpoints.
On pieces in $[-1/2,1/2]$, evaluate its alternating power series. For positive
pieces in $[1/2,1]$, use
$\arctan t=\pi/4-\arctan((1-t)/(1+t))$; in $[1,3]$, use
$\arctan t=\pi/4+\arctan((t-1)/(t+1))$; for $t\ge3$, use
$\arctan t=\pi/2-\arctan(1/t)$. Evaluate negative pieces by odd symmetry. Form each reduced interval by
exact rational endpoint formulas and evaluate its polynomial and symmetric
tail by exact rational interval arithmetic before outward conversion; every
reduced argument lies in $[-1/2,1/2]$. Combine the converted enclosure with
the fixed $\pi$ enclosure by outward arithmetic. Enclose $\pi$ using Machin's identity and the alternating series at $1/5$ and
$1/239$, forming rational partial sums and tail endpoints exactly before
final outward conversion. If every piece is finite, take the interval hull of
all piece enclosures. If any branch test or piece is unresolved, return its
non-finite status with that piece and do not use a partial hull.

4. For each sine or cosine node, first compute one outward Machin interval
$P_N$ for $\pi$ using the same $N$ and format, combining the rational series
endpoints exactly before final outward conversion. If $P_N$ is non-finite or
its lower endpoint is not positive, return `inconclusive`. For finite input
$X=[a,b]$, put $M_X=\max(|a|,|b|)$, $p_-:=\inf(P_N)>0$, and
$K=\lceil2M_X/p_-\rceil+1$, with the ceiling computed by exact rational
comparisons. If the width of $X$ is at least $2\sup(P_N)$, outward-round the
exact endpoints $-1$ and $1$; if either conversion overflows, return
`overflow` with the node and input interval, and otherwise return the resulting
interval. Otherwise examine the finite candidate list $k=-K,\ldots,K$ for
the canonical cells $[k\pi/2-\pi/4,k\pi/2+\pi/4]$. For each candidate form
the exact rational interval enclosure
$C_k=kP_N/2+[-1/4,1/4]P_N$ of its canonical cell. For $k>K$, the exact
left endpoint $(2k-1)\pi/4$ of cell $k$ is at least
$(2k-1)p_-/4>M_X$; for $k<-K$, its exact right endpoint
$-(2|k|-1)\pi/4$ is at most $-(2|k|-1)p_-/4<-M_X$. Thus no omitted exact
cell can intersect $X$. Include each candidate whose $C_k$ intersects $X$;
exclude only candidates whose intersection is empty by exact comparison. Let
$X_k$ be the exact interval hull of $X\cap C_k$, without rounding these
endpoints, and form the residual enclosure $R_k=X_k-kP_N/2$. Certify
$R_k\subseteq[-1,1]$, evaluate the sine polynomial through degree $2N+1$ or
the cosine polynomial through degree $2N$, and add the corresponding explicit
geometric tail from [[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]]
by exact rational interval arithmetic. For $j\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ the
quarter-period map for a sine node is respectively
$\sin r,\cos r,-\sin r,-\cos r$, and for a cosine node it is respectively
$\cos r,-\sin r,-\cos r,\sin r$, where $j$ is the least nonnegative residue
of $k$ modulo $4$. For a negative sign, negate the interval and reverse its
endpoints. Intersect each mapped enclosure with $[-1,1]$. Round the final
endpoints outward and take the hull over every included cell.
If no candidate is included, a cell cannot be certified in the reduced
interval, or any candidate endpoint overflows, return `inconclusive` or
`overflow` with the cell; never omit that piece from a finite hull.

For tangent, form the same finite canonical-cell list even when the input width
meets the wide-input shortcut; do not use that shortcut. For each included cell
$k$, form its reduced input interval $R_k$ as above and evaluate sine and
cosine on that cell. Divide their enclosures only when the cosine enclosure
excludes zero. Otherwise, for odd $k$, form the exact dyadic pole enclosure
$K_k=kP_N/2$. If $K_k$ is contained in the cell's input intersection, then
$k\pi/2$ lies in that cell and is a cosine zero, so return `split-domain` with
the cell. If the cosine enclosure contains zero but this pole test does not
certify a zero, return `inconclusive` with the cell. Take the interval hull of
tangent enclosures only when every piece is finite.

5. For complex exponential on $X+iY$, evaluate real $\exp(X)$, $\cos(Y)$,
and $\sin(Y)$ and combine their enclosures by rectangle operations. For
principal $\operatorname{Log}$, first require a rectangle excluding zero and
every point of the negative real branch cut; otherwise return `domain-error`.
Compute an outward Machin interval $P_N$ for $\pi$ using this call's $N$ and
format; if it is non-finite or its lower endpoint is not positive, return
`inconclusive`.
Split each coordinate interval into its nonempty strictly negative and
strictly positive portions, plus the singleton $\{0\}$ when it contains zero.
Use the closures of the strictly signed portions as interval enclosures; form
their Cartesian products for the quadrant pieces, and handle products with an
axis singleton separately. Omit empty pieces. These finitely many pieces
cover the rectangle, with quadrant closures allowed to overlap their axis
pieces. On a quadrant where the denominator interval excludes zero, use
$$\operatorname{Arg}(x+iy)= \begin{cases} \arctan(y/x),&x>0,\ y>0,\\ -\arctan((-y)/x),&x>0,\ y<0,\\ \pi-\arctan(y/(-x)),&x<0,\ y>0,\\ -\pi+\arctan((-y)/(-x)),&x<0,\ y<0. \end{cases}$$
Write this call's fixed interval as $P_N=[p_-,p_+]$ and form the exact
dyadic sector intervals
$$S_{\rm I}=[0,p_+/2],\qquad S_{\rm II}=[p_-/2,p_+],\qquad S_{\rm III}=[-p_+,-p_-/2],\qquad S_{\rm IV}=[-p_+/2,0].$$
For every ratio-based quadrant piece, obtain its finite real arctangent
enclosure by the real rules above; propagate any non-finite result. Form the
full argument interval $A$ in the displayed quadrant formula by exact
rational endpoint arithmetic, using this same $P_N$ for each occurrence of
$\pi$. Before final outward conversion or hull formation, replace $A$ by
$J=A\cap S_q$, where $q$ is that piece's quadrant. Compute the intersection
by exact endpoint maxima and minima. If it is empty, return `inconclusive`
with the piece and status `empty-argument-intersection`; do not omit the
piece. If the denominator interval has a zero endpoint, use $J=S_q$
instead of a ratio formula.

For an interval $J=[a,b]$ produced by either branch, apply the same final
conversion $H(J)=[\operatorname{rd}(a),\operatorname{ru}(b)]$ in the selected
format. Perform this conversion after intersection for a ratio branch and
after selecting $S_q$ for a coarse branch. Finite subnormal endpoints are
accepted; an overflow returns `overflow` with the piece. On the positive
imaginary axis use $H(P_N/2)$, on the negative imaginary axis use
$H(-P_N/2)$, and on the positive real axis use $H([0,0])$. The initial domain
check excludes the origin and negative real axis, so these are all remaining
axis cases.

On each piece enclose $\ln\sqrt{X^2+Y^2}$ using the real operations and
evaluator, and combine it with the converted argument interval into a
rectangle. If every piece is finite, take the coordinatewise hull of all
piece rectangles. If any piece, conversion or branch is unresolved, return
its status and piece without forming a partial hull.

Every finite interval returned for a requested real output node by
[[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] on an input interval in the
domain of $\exp$, $\ln$, $\sqrt{\phantom{x}}$, $\arctan$, $\sin$, $\cos$, or
$\tan$ contains the exact range of the corresponding function on that
interval. For the same typed DAG and designated real output node, if all
input intervals are nested coordinatewise, all constant enclosures are fixed,
and both calls use the same finite dyadic format and truncation index $N$,
then, whenever both calls return finite enclosures, the canonical branch-cell
and fixed-term construction makes the smaller domain's computed enclosure a
subset of the larger one's.
An unresolved fixed branch, pole, invalid domain or overflow returns its
stated non-finite status and carries no finite success claim.

For finite $x$ with $|x|\le N_{\max}$, the directed roundings defined in
[[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]] satisfy
$\operatorname{rd}(x)\le x\le\operatorname{ru}(x)$ and each endpoint error is
at most the stated $\epsilon_{\rm abs}(x)$ (with zero error when $x$ is
representable). For $x>N_{\max}$ the pair $(N_{\max},+\infty)$ encloses $x$;
for $x<-N_{\max}$ the pair $(-\infty,-N_{\max})$ encloses $x$. Overflow has
error bound $+\infty$ and cannot be reported as a finite-error result.

For $|u|\le1/2$ and integer $N\ge1$, set
$E_N(u)=\sum_{k=0}^N u^k/k!$ and
$R_E=|u|^{N+1}/((N+1)!(1-|u|/(N+2)))$. Then
$\exp(u)\in[E_N(u)-R_E,E_N(u)+R_E]$, and the lower endpoint is positive.
For $y\in[1,2]$, put $v=(y-1)/(y+1)$ and
$L_N(v)=2\sum_{k=0}^N v^{2k+1}/(2k+1)$. Then
$$\left|\ln y-L_N(v)\right|\le \frac{2|v|^{2N+3}}{(2N+3)(1-v^2)}.$$
For every integer $j$ and $y>0$, the natural logarithm also satisfies
$\ln(2^j y)=j\ln2+\ln y$.
For $|t|\le1/2$, set $A_N(t)=\sum_{k=0}^N(-1)^kt^{2k+1}/(2k+1)$. Then
$$\left|\arctan t-A_N(t)\right|\le \frac{|t|^{2N+3}}{(2N+3)(1-t^2)}.$$

derivations.claim: For every reproduction pmf $q$, including boundary points of the simplex, define $G(W,q):=\sum_i p_iD(W(\cdot|i)\|q)+\beta\mathbb E d$, where a row divergence is $+\infty$ if that row puts positive mass outside the support of $q$. Since each $p_i>0$, $G(W,q)$ is finite only when every row is supported on $\{j:q(j)>0\}$. Also $Z_i(q)>0$ for every pmf $q$, because $e^{-\beta d_{ij}}>0$ and $q$ has total mass one. Define $W_q(j|i)=q(j)e^{-\beta d_{ij}}/Z_i(q)$, which is zero off that support. For every supported row, expansion of finite KL sums gives $$D(W(\cdot|i)\|q)+\beta\sum_jW(j|i)d_{ij}=D(W(\cdot|i)\|W_q(\cdot|i))-\ln Z_i(q).$$ Nonnegativity [F3] shows that $W_q$ minimizes each row; unsupported rows have infinite objective and cannot improve it. Therefore $F(q):=\min_WG(W,q)=-\sum_i p_i\ln Z_i(q)$ on the closed simplex. If $q_W$ is the output law of $W$, expansion on the common support gives $G(W,q)=L_\beta(W)+D(q_W\|q)$ when $q_W$ is supported on $q$; otherwise both sides are $+\infty$.

Fix an integer $t$. The recurrence through $t$ is a finite expression DAG with positive exact divisors and logarithm arguments, since every iterate has full support. The algorithm uses mantissa precision $r^2$, exponent bounds $-r,r$, and truncation $N=r$. Uniformly for each endpoint $x$ in a fixed bounded input interval, the evaluator in [F6] uses $s=r+2$ squarings after reducing to $u=x/2^s$. On a fixed bounded neighborhood of $x$, [F7] bounds the initial series error by $C^{r+1}2^{-s(r+1)}/(r+1)!$ for some fixed $C\ge1$, and the endpoint rounding error by $O(2^{-r^2})$. The exact intermediate exponentials are uniformly bounded; on a fixed larger bounded interval, squaring is Lipschitz with some fixed constant $A>1$. Thus the total endpoint error after $s$ rounded squarings is at most $A^{r+2}$ times the initial error plus $O(A^{r+2}2^{-r^2})$, which tends to zero. The exact exponential is Lipschitz on that interval, so a shrinking input interval has a shrinking output enclosure. This bound also ensures the rounded intermediates remain in that larger interval for all sufficiently large $r$. Logarithm range reduction on a fixed positive compact interval uses only finitely many bins; its series tails tend to zero, and its endpoint operations are continuous there. Rational input rounding likewise converges by [F7]. Applying these bounds successively to the finite recurrence DAG shows every requested enclosure width tends to zero. All exact positive divisors and logarithm arguments are eventually separated from zero, and the expanding exponent range eventually avoids overflow. The finite maximum forming $G_t$ preserves convergence, so its logarithm enclosure also shrinks to $\ln\gamma_t$. Soundness follows from [F6]. Hence each fixed-$t$ precision loop terminates with the required width.

The channel simplex is closed and bounded in finite-dimensional Euclidean space, hence compact by [F4]. The finite mutual-information objective is continuous by its entropy expression and continuity of $-u\ln u$ at zero; distortion is linear. Thus [F5] gives a minimizer $W^*$. Put $q^*=q_{W^*}$, $P^*(i,j)=p_iW^*(j|i)$. Step 1.1 gives $G(W,q)\ge L_\beta(W)\ge L_\beta^*$ for every $W,q$, while $G(W^*,q^*)=L_\beta^*$ because $q^*$ is the output marginal of $W^*$. Therefore $F(q^*)=L_\beta^*$ and $q^*$ minimizes the boundary-extended $F$.

For each iterate set $P_t(i,j)=p_iW_t(j|i)$. The identities in step 1.1 give $$ F(q_t)=L_t+D(q_{t+1}\|q_t),\qquad F(q_{t+1})\le G(W_t,q_{t+1})=L_t. $$ Consequently $L_{t+1}\le F(q_{t+1})\le L_t$: the objective sequence is nonincreasing.

Expand the finite joint divergence using the update formula for $W_t$: $$ D(P^*\|P_t)=L_\beta^*+D(q^*\|q_t)-F(q_t). $$ Indeed $\ln W_t(j|i)=\ln q_t(j)-\beta d_{ij}-\ln Z_i(q_t)$; multiplying $\ln(W^*/W_t)$ by $p_iW^*_{ij}$ and summing gives the displayed identity. Marginalizing the joint laws over the reproduction coordinate and expanding the finite conditional sums gives $$ D(P^*\|P_t)=D(q^*\|q_{t+1})+\sum_{j:q^*_j>0}q^*_jD(P^*(X\in\cdot\mid j)\|P_t(X\in\cdot\mid j))\ge D(q^*\|q_{t+1}), $$ where [F3] supplies nonnegativity. Thus $F(q_t)-L_\beta^*\le D(q^*\|q_t)-D(q^*\|q_{t+1})$. Since $L_t\le F(q_t)$, the same upper bound holds for $L_t-L_\beta^*$.

Define $s_j(q_t)=\sum_i p_i e^{-\beta d_{ij}}/Z_i(q_t)=q_{t+1,j}/q_{t,j}$. For $a_{ij}=e^{-\beta d_{ij}}/Z_i(q_t)$, concavity of $\ln$ and $F(q^*)=L_\beta^*$ give $$ F(q_t)-L_\beta^*=\sum_i p_i\ln\left(\sum_jq_j^*a_{ij}\right) \le\ln\left(\sum_jq_j^*s_j(q_t)\right)\le\ln\max_js_j(q_t)=\ln\gamma_t. $$ Since $L_t\le F(q_t)$, this proves the stated a-posteriori certificate. Also $\sum_jq_{t,j}s_j(q_t)=1$, so $\gamma_t\ge1$.

Summing step 3.1 for $s=0,\ldots,t$ telescopes to $\sum_{s=0}^t(L_s-L_\beta^*)\le D(q^*\|q_0)$, since KL is nonnegative. By step 2.2 the gaps are nonincreasing, so $(t+1)(L_t-L_\beta^*)\le D(q^*\|q_0)$. If $q_0$ is uniform, $D(q^*\|q_0)=\ln n-H(q^*)\le\ln n$.

The sequence $F(q_t)$ is nonincreasing by step 2.2 and bounded below by $L_\beta^*$. Moreover, $F(q_t)-F(q_{t+1})\ge D(q_{t+1}\|q_t)$, so this successive KL divergence tends to zero. Step 4.1 gives $L_t\to L_\beta^*$; the first identity in step 2.2 then gives $F(q_t)\to L_\beta^*$. The simplex is compact, and $F$, each $s_j$, and $\gamma$ are continuous there because every $Z_i(q)\ge\min_j e^{-\beta d_{ij}}>0$. Every cluster point of $q_t$ is therefore a minimizer of $F$.

At any minimizer $q$ of differentiable $F(q)=-\sum_i p_i\ln Z_i(q)$, the coordinate derivative is $-s_j(q)$. Moving mass between a positive coordinate and any other coordinate shows $s_j(q)=1$ on the support and $s_j(q)\le1$ off the support; the active value equals one because $\sum_jq_js_j(q)=1$. Hence $\gamma(q)=1$ at every minimizer. Compactness and continuity from step 5.1 imply $\gamma_t\to1$: otherwise a subsequence bounded away from one would have a cluster point with the same property. By step 1.2, the enclosure upper endpoints satisfy $u_t\le\ln\gamma_t+1/(t+1)$, so $u_t\to0$ and every positive tolerance is eventually met. The argument permits zero coordinates in $q^*$, so boundary minimizers are included.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $X_0,X_1,\ldots$ be a source over a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. For positive integers $n$ and $M_n$, write $[M_n]=\{1,\ldots,M_n\}$. An $n$-block fixed-length code with $M_n$ messages is a deterministic encoder $f_n:\mathcal X^n\to[M_n]$ and decoder $g_n:[M_n]\to\widehat{\mathcal X}^{\,n}$; its reconstruction is $\widehat X^n=g_n(f_n(X^n))$, its block distortion is [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]], and its rate is $n^{-1}\log_2M_n$ bits per source symbol.

For each $D\ge0$, define the expected-distortion operational rate $R_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{avg}}(D)$ as the infimum of $\limsup_n n^{-1}\log_2M_n$ over code sequences satisfying $\limsup_n\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)\le D$. Define the positive-slack excess-distortion operational rate $R_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{slack}}(D)$ by the same rate infimum over code sequences satisfying

$$\text{for every }\varepsilon>0,\qquad \mathbb P\!\left(d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)>D+\varepsilon\right)\longrightarrow0.$$

The infimum of an empty set of admissible code sequences is $+\infty$. The expected and positive-slack excess criteria are separate definitions. An exact-threshold condition $\mathbb P(d_n>D)\to0$ is not part of either definition.

Let $(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a stationary source on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$ be a bounded finite-valued distortion. For $n\ge1$ and $D\ge0$, define
$$
R_n(D):=\frac{1}{n\ln2}\min_{W_n:\,\mathbb E d_n(X_0^{n-1},\widehat X_0^{n-1})\le D} I(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1})\quad\text{bits/symbol},
$$
with value $+\infty$ when the constraint is infeasible. The minimum is attained whenever feasible by [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]] applied to the block alphabets. Put
$$
D_{\min}:=\mathbb E\min_{\hat x\in\widehat{\mathcal X}}d(X_0,\hat x),\qquad D_{\rm c}:=\min_{\hat x\in\widehat{\mathcal X}}\mathbb E d(X_0,\hat x),\qquad R_{\rm block}(D):=\inf_{n\ge1}R_n(D).
$$
The stationary-ergodic process information rate-distortion quantity is
$$
R_{\rm erg}(D):=\inf \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n\ln2} I(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1}),
$$
where the infimum ranges over jointly stationary ergodic pairs of finite-alphabet processes with the given source marginal and $\mathbb E d(X_0,\widehat X_0)\le D$; an empty infimum is $+\infty$.

For a stationary finite-alphabet source and bounded additive distortion as in [[def-it-stationary-finite-block-information-rdf]], the sequence $R_n(D)$ has a limit for every feasible $D$, and
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}R_n(D)=\inf_{n\ge1}R_n(D)=R_{\rm block}(D).
$$
The function $R_{\rm block}$ is nonincreasing and convex on $[D_{\min},\infty)$, is zero for $D\ge D_{\rm c}$, and is right-continuous at $D_{\min}$. It is infinite for $0\le D<D_{\min}$.

Assume AC. $$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n I_2(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1})<r\quad\text{bits per symbol},
$$
where $I_2:=I_{\rm nat}/\ln2$ for the measure-theoretic mutual information of [[def-measure-theoretic-mutual-information]].
For a stationary ergodic finite-alphabet source, the componentwise information-rate limit is the constant entropy rate.

Let $\mu$ be sigma-finite, let $T$ preserve $\mu$, and let $f$ be a
finite-valued real- or complex-valued measurable representative in
$\mathcal L^1(\mu)$.  Then $A_nf$ converges $\mu$-almost everywhere to a
finite-valued integrable function $f^*$ satisfying

$$f^*\circ T=f^*\quad\mu\text{-almost everywhere},\qquad \lVert f^*\rVert_1\leq\lVert f\rVert_1.$$

The a.e. class of $f^*$ depends only on the a.e. class of $f$.  No ergodicity,
finite total measure, completeness, or invertibility is assumed.

Let $X,Y,Z$ have a joint pmf on finite alphabets and suppose that, for every $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$,

$$p_{XZ|y}(x,z)=p_{X|y}(x)p_{Z|y}(z).$$

This is the finite Markov condition $X\to Y\to Z$. Then

$$I(X;Z)\le I(X;Y),$$

with equality if and only if $I(X;Y|Z)=0$, equivalently $X$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given every positive-mass value of $Z$.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.
Proves that n^{-1}H(X_0,...,X_{n-1}) converges under stationarity and equals the limit of the finite-past conditional entropies.

Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

derivations.claim: For any source word $x_0^{n-1}$, every reconstruction word satisfies $$ d_n(x_0^{n-1},\hat x_0^{n-1})\ge\frac1n\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\min_{\hat x}d(x_i,\hat x). $$ The right side has expectation $D_{\min}$ by stationarity, so every code has expected distortion at least $D_{\min}$. If $D<D_{\min}$, choose $\epsilon>0$ with $D+\epsilon<D_{\min}$ and put $g(X)=\min_{\hat x}d(X,\hat x)$. Birkhoff [F6] gives almost-sure convergence of the averages of this bounded function to a finite invariant function $g^*$. For every rational $a$, the limsup orbit set $\limsup_{n\to\infty}T^{-n}\{g^*>a\}$ is strictly invariant and differs from $\{g^*>a\}$ by a null set. Ergodicity makes each such level set have probability zero or one, so $g^*$ is constant almost surely. Dominated convergence and stationarity identify the constant as $\mathbb E g=D_{\min}$. Hence the pointwise-minimum block average converges almost surely to $D_{\min}$, and the probability that any code's distortion exceeds $D+\epsilon$ tends to one. Both operational criteria are therefore infeasible below $D_{\min}$. By [F2], no stationary coupling with mean distortion below $D_{\min}$ exists either, so $R_{\rm erg}(D)=+\infty$; [F3] gives $R_{\rm block}(D)=+\infty$.

Let a deterministic length-$n$ code have $M_n$ messages and reconstruction $\widehat X^n$. Since $X^n\to f_n(X^n)\to\widehat X^n$ is a Markov chain, [F7] gives $I(X^n;\widehat X^n)\le H(f_n(X^n))\le\log_2M_n$. Its induced joint law is feasible in the definition of $R_n(D_n)$, where $D_n=\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)$, so $R_n(D_n)\le n^{-1}\log_2M_n$.

For every jointly stationary ergodic pair feasible at $D$, the finite-block law is feasible in $R_n(D)$, so $R_n(D)\le n^{-1}I_2(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1})$. Taking limits and then the infimum over such pairs gives $R_{\rm block}(D)\le R_{\rm erg}(D)$.

For expected-distortion codes with $\limsup D_n\le D$, eventually $D_n\le D+\epsilon$, giving $R_n(D+\epsilon)\le n^{-1}\log_2M_n$. For a positive-slack excess code, boundedness gives $D_n\le D+\epsilon+d_{\max}\mathbb P(d_n>D+\epsilon)$, so eventually $D_n\le D+2\epsilon$; then $R_n(D+2\epsilon)\le n^{-1}\log_2M_n$. Taking limits and using [F3], followed by right-continuity as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, proves $R_{\rm block}(D)\le R_{\rm op}^{\rm avg}(D)$ and $R_{\rm block}(D)\le R_{\rm op}^{\rm slack}(D)$.

Conversely, for any bit rate $r>R_{\rm block}(D)$, [F4] supplies a jointly stationary ergodic pair with mean distortion at most $D$ and limsup bit mutual-information rate less than $r$. Thus $R_{\rm erg}(D)\le r$; letting $r\downarrow R_{\rm block}(D)$ proves $R_{\rm erg}(D)=R_{\rm block}(D)$.

Fix a jointly stationary ergodic pair $(X,\widehat X)$ supplied by step 2.2. By [F8], each of the source, reproduction, and joint-pair normalized block entropies has a limit; [F9] therefore gives convergence of $n^{-1}I_2(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1})$ to a finite bit rate $\bar I\le\limsup n^{-1}I_2(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1})<r$. By [F5] applied to those three stationary ergodic processes, their normalized negative log probabilities in bits converge almost surely to their entropy rates. Subtracting the three limits shows that the information density $$ i_n(x^n;\hat x^n):=\log_2\frac{P_{\widehat X^n|X^n}(\hat x^n|x^n)}{P_{\widehat X^n}(\hat x^n)} $$ divided by $n$ converges almost surely to $h(X)+h(\widehat X)-h(X,\widehat X)=\bar I$, with each entropy rate in bits.

On the ergodic pair shift let $g=d(X_0,\widehat X_0)$. By [F6], its time averages converge almost surely to a finite invariant function $g^*$. Apply the rational-level-set argument from step 1.1 to this bounded function on the ergodic pair system; its limit is constant, and dominated convergence with stationarity identifies that constant as $\bar d:=\mathbb E d(X_0,\widehat X_0)\le D$. Thus $d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)\to\bar d$ almost surely. Fix $\eta>0$ and $\delta>0$. The event $$ G_n:=\{d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)\le D+\eta,\ i_n(X^n;\widehat X^n)\le n(\bar I+\delta)\} $$ has probability tending to one by step 3.1 and this distortion convergence. Hence the set of source words whose conditional probability of this event is at least $1/2$ has source probability tending to one: its complement probability is at most twice $\mathbb P(G_n^c)$.

For any such source word $x^n$, on its good reproduction set the likelihood ratio $P_{\widehat X^n|x^n}/P_{\widehat X^n}$ is at most $2^{n(\bar I+\delta)}$. Therefore an independent reproduction word sampled from $P_{\widehat X^n}$ lands in that set with probability at least $\frac12 2^{-n(\bar I+\delta)}$. Draw $M_n=\lceil2^{n(\bar I+2\delta)}\rceil$ independent reproduction words. The probability that none works for this source word is at most $(1-q)^{M_n}\le e^{-M_nq}\le e^{-2^{n\delta}/2}$. Averaging over source words shows the expected failure probability of the random codebook tends to zero.

Some deterministic realization of each random codebook has failure probability at most twice its ensemble mean (if the mean is zero, choose a realization with zero failure). Encode a source word by the first codeword satisfying the good conditions, and use a fixed default reproduction if none does. The decoder outputs the selected codeword, so the code is deterministic and has $M_n$ messages. On success its distortion is at most $D+\eta$; on failure it is at most $d_{\max}$.

To obtain expected distortion at most $D$ in the limit and positive-slack excess distortion, choose a decreasing sequence $\eta_j\downarrow0$. For each $j$, the failure probability in step 6.1 is at most $1/j$ for all sufficiently large $n$; choose increasing thresholds and at each length use the largest such $j=j(n)$ available. Then $j(n)\to\infty$, expected distortion is at most $D+\eta_{j(n)}+d_{\max}/j(n)$, and for every fixed slack $\epsilon>0$, eventually $\eta_{j(n)}<\epsilon$, so $\mathbb P(d_n>D+\epsilon)\le1/j(n)\to0$. The code rate has limsup at most $\bar I+2\delta$.

Given any target rate $R_{\rm block}(D)+\epsilon$, choose $r=R_{\rm block}(D)+\epsilon/3$. Step 2.2 gives $\bar I<r$, so choose $\delta>0$ with $\bar I+2\delta<R_{\rm block}(D)+\epsilon$. Steps 5.1, 6.1 and 7.1 give both operational criteria at rate below the target. Thus $R_{\rm op}^{\rm avg}(D)\le R_{\rm block}(D)$ and $R_{\rm op}^{\rm slack}(D)\le R_{\rm block}(D)$. Together with steps 2.1 and 2.2 this proves all equalities. The excess criterion used positive slack throughout; it does not imply the unclaimed exact-threshold assertion at $D_{\min}$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be standard-Borel spaces, let $P_X$ be a probability law on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable. A feasible joint law, or coupling, is a probability measure $\pi$ on $\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}$ whose $\mathcal X$-marginal is $P_X$. For each distortion budget $D\ge0$, define

$$R_{\mathrm{std}}(D):=\inf_{\substack{\pi_{\mathcal X}=P_X\\ \int d\,d\pi\le D}}\frac{D(\pi\|P_X\otimes\pi_{\widehat{\mathcal X}})}{\ln2}=\inf_{\substack{\pi_{\mathcal X}=P_X\\ \int d\,d\pi\le D}}\frac{I_{\mathrm{nat}}(X;\widehat X)}{\ln2}.$$

The infimum of an empty feasible set is $+\infty$. Values are in bits. This definition makes no general existence or attainment claim and supplies no operational coding theorem for arbitrary standard-Borel alphabets.

Assume AC. Let $X,Y$ be random elements with standard-Borel value spaces $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ and $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)$, and let $P_{XY}$, $P_X$, and $P_Y$ be their joint and marginal probability laws. The product law $P_X\otimes P_Y$ exists by [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]]. Define the mutual information in nats by

$$I_{\mathrm{nat}}(X;Y):=D(P_{XY}\|P_X\otimes P_Y)\in[0,+\infty],$$

where $D$ is the directional Kullback–Leibler divergence of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. This definition remains meaningful when one or both laws have no Lebesgue density and does not subtract differential entropies that may be infinite.

$$\phi_i(\delta_i):=\begin{cases}\frac12\log_2(\lambda_i/\delta_i),&\lambda_i>0,\ 0<\delta_i\le\lambda_i,\\+\infty,&\lambda_i>0,\ \delta_i=0,\\0,&\lambda_i=0,\ \delta_i=0.\end{cases}$$

$$\sum_i\min(\lambda_i,\theta)=D,$$

$$\frac12\sum_i\log_2^+(\lambda_i/\theta),\qquad \delta_i^*=\min(\lambda_i,\theta),$$

$$0\le \frac{\log s}{s}=\frac1s\int_1^s\frac{du}{u}\le\frac1s\int_1^s\frac{du}{\sqrt u}\le\frac2{\sqrt s}.$$
Thus $t\log t\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$; here $L=\log$ by
[[cor-integral-logarithm-agrees-with-natural-logarithm]] and
[[def-integral-logarithm]]. On $(0,\infty)$, $\psi$ is a product of continuous
functions by [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]] and
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], so $\psi$ is continuous on
$[0,\infty)$ and $\psi(r)$ is measurable by
[[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]. Its signed integral is
defined by the positive and negative parts
([[def-positive-and-negative-parts-of-a-function]],
[[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]]).

For $0<t\le1$, the function $-t\log t$ has derivative $-\log t-1$ and
maximum $1/e$ at $t=1/e$: $e=\exp(1)>1$ by
[[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]] and
[[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]], $1/e=\exp(-1)$ by
[[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], and $\log(1/e)=-1$ by
[[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]] and the inverse definition. The mean value
theorem gives increase before and decrease after this point
([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-integral-logarithm-derivative-and-normalisation]],
[[cor-integral-logarithm-agrees-with-natural-logarithm]], [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]).
At $t=0$ the negative part is zero. Since $Q$ is a probability measure,
$$\int \psi(r)^-\,dQ\le\frac1e.$$
The change-of-measure identity of [[thm-likelihood-ratio-change-of-measure]],
applied to $\ell^-$ gives $\int\ell^-\,dP=\int\psi(r)^-\,dQ\le1/e$,
so $\int\ell\,dP$ is well-defined; applying it to both positive and negative
parts gives
$$D(P\|Q)=\int\ell\,dP=\int\psi(r)\,dQ=\int r\log r\,dQ,$$
with $0\log0:=0$ and a finite negative part. Therefore the extended integral
is well-defined without an $\infty-\infty$ ambiguity.

Assume AC. Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. By [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]] and [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]], gamma is a probability measure; denote it $N(0,1)$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$. This affine map is continuous: for $\sigma$>0 choose $\delta$=$\varepsilon$/$\sigma$, and for $\sigma$=0 it is constant. Its inverse images of opens are open, so it is Borel measurable. [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]] makes its pushforward a probability. When $\sigma$=0, the preimage of E is all of R if m belongs to E and empty otherwise, so $N(m,0)=\delta_m$ in [[def-dirac-measure]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, let $Z\sim N_n(0,I_n)$ have independent standard-normal coordinates, and let $U\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ satisfy $U^TU=I_n$. Then $UZ$ also has independent $N(0,1)$ coordinates. Here $I_n$ is the identity matrix and $U$ is orthogonal.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces. Then:

1. the set function $E \mapsto (\mu \times \nu)(E)$ of
   [[def-product-measure-on-sigma-finite-spaces]] is a measure on
   $\mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B$;
2. for measurable rectangles,
   $$(\mu \times \nu)(A \times B)=\mu(A)\nu(B),$$
   with the nonnegative extended-product convention $0\cdot\infty=\infty\cdot0=0$;
3. the measure $\mu \times \nu$ is sigma-finite; and
4. it is the unique measure on $\mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B$ with the
   rectangle formula.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

By [F1]–[F2], $$ R(5/2)=\frac12\left(\log_2\frac4{3/2}+\log_2^+\frac1{3/2}\right)=\frac12\log_2\frac83. $$

Put $a=\sqrt{5/2}$ and $b=\sqrt{3/2}$. Choose independent standard normals $U,V,X_2$ by [F5], and set $X_1=aU+bV$, $Y_1=aU$, $Y_2=0$. The matrix with rows $(a,b)/2$ and $(b,-a)/2$ is orthogonal, so [F4] gives $X_1\sim N(0,4)$, independently of $X_2$. The errors are $bV$ and $X_2$, with total mean square $b^2+1=5/2$.

Write $f_s(t)=(2\pi s)^{-1/2}\exp(-t^2/(2s))$ for the $N(0,s)$ density. By [F4]–[F6], $(X_1,Y_1)$ has density $f_{a^2}(y)f_{b^2}(x-y)$. Relative to Lebesgue measure in $(x_1,x_2,y_1)$ times the point mass at $y_2=0$, the joint law and product of the marginals therefore have respective positive densities $f_{a^2}(y_1)f_{b^2}(x_1-y_1)f_1(x_2)$ and $f_4(x_1)f_1(x_2)f_{a^2}(y_1)$. Their log ratio is $$\frac12\ln\frac4{b^2}-\frac{(x_1-y_1)^2}{2b^2}+\frac{x_1^2}{8}.$$ It is integrable since both quadratic terms have finite expectations. By [F3] and step 1.2 its joint expectation is $\frac12\ln(8/3)-\frac12+\frac12=\frac12\ln(8/3)$ nats. Dividing by $\ln2$ yields the rate in step 1.1, proving attainment without assuming a Lebesgue density for the constant reconstruction coordinate.
